A third MCU Spider-Man film was planned during the production of *Homecoming* in 2017. Negotiations between Sony and Marvel Studios to alter their deal—in which they produce the Spider-Man films together—ended with Marvel Studios leaving the project in August 2019, but a negative fan reaction led to a new deal between the companies a month later. Watts, McKenna, Sommers, and Holland were set to return, and filming took place from October 2020 to March 2021 in New York City and Atlanta. *No Way Home* serves as a [crossover](/wiki/Crossover_(fiction) "Crossover (fiction)") between the MCU and the previous [*Spider-Man* films](/wiki/Spider-Man_in_film "Spider-Man in film") directed by [Sam Raimi](/wiki/Sam_Raimi "Sam Raimi") and [Marc Webb](/wiki/Marc_Webb "Marc Webb"). Several actors reprise their roles from those films, including previous Spider-Man actors Maguire and Garfield. The pair's involvement was the subject of wide speculation and numerous leaks despite Sony, Marvel, and the cast's efforts to conceal their involvement until the film's release.

*Spider-Man: No Way Home* premiered at the [Fox Village Theater](/wiki/Fox_Village_Theater "Fox Village Theater") in [Westwood, Los Angeles](/wiki/Westwood,_Los_Angeles "Westwood, Los Angeles"), on December 13, 2021, and was theatrically released in the United States on December 17, as part of [Phase Four](/wiki/Marvel_Cinematic_Universe:_Phase_Four "Marvel Cinematic Universe: Phase Four") of the MCU. fanoutqa_039324.x:
David Card :: Contributions to Economics of Education :: chunk_0003
David Card has made influential contributions to the economics of education by studying how access and school environments affect long-term outcomes. In one of his studies, Card used proximity to colleges as an instrumental variable. Results showed that people who lived closer to universities were more likely to enroll. Because of the additional years of schooling, this translated into higher earnings.[[19]](#cite_note-:2-19) Card’s work helped prove that there are other factors that affect earnings and play a key role, like schooling. He also found that smaller class sizes, staff income, and resources can affect students' prospects, especially for those from disadvantaged backgrounds.[[23]](#cite_note-23) His findings encouraged economists to consider how educational environments can affect inequality over time, and his studies helped broaden how economists think about education by highlighting the importance of real-world variation, institutional differences, and student experiences. His work played an important role in shifting the field toward a more careful empirical design and helped establish education as an area where credible causal evidence could be used to understand economic mobility and opportunity. These contributions were part of a broader empirical movement recognized when Card received the 2021 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics Sciences.[[6]](#cite_note-:0-6)[[8]](#cite_note-:1-8)

Rain of flightless animals and things has been reported throughout history.[[1]](#cite_note-Library_of_Congress-1) In the [Bible](/wiki/Bible "Bible"), a rain of frogs is described as one of the [ten plagues of Egypt](/wiki/Plagues_of_Egypt "Plagues of Egypt"). The Bible also mentions other similar events, such as [quail](/wiki/Quail "Quail") falling from the sky to save the Hebrews from hunger in Exodus 16:13. In the fourth century BC, the Greek [Athenaeus](/wiki/Athenaeus "Athenaeus") mentioned a rain of fish that lasted three days in the region of [Chaeronea](/wiki/Chaeronea "Chaeronea") in the [Peloponnese](/wiki/Peloponnese "Peloponnese").[[4]](#cite_note-:1-4) In the [Middle Ages](/wiki/Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), the frequency of the phenomenon in certain regions led locals to imagine that fish were born in the skies before falling into the sea.[[4]](#cite_note-:1-4)

* In 1935, during the Japanese invasion of China, the university fell under Japanese control.
